Title: Introduction to Digital Humanities | Harvard University
# Introduction to Digital Humanities. Develop skills in digital research and visualization techniques across subjects and fields within the humanities. * How common digital tools work and examples of projects using them. * How various file types can be used to create, gather, and organize data. * How to use command-line functions to analyze text. * How to use free tools to create visual text analysis. As museums, libraries, archives and other institutions have digitized collections and artifacts, new tools and standards have been developed that turn those materials into machine-readable data. Optical Character Recognition (OCR) and the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI), for example, have enabled humanities researchers to process vast amounts of textual data. This course will show you how to manage the many aspects of digital humanities research and scholarship. Whether you are a student or scholar, librarian or archivist, museum curator or public historian — or just plain curious — this course will help you bring your area of study or interest to new life using digital tools. * Describe the implicit and explicit hierarchies that are created when gathering and analyzing data. * Distinguish between what counts as data and what does not. * Identify different data formats and how they fit into a research workflow. Digital Humanities Projects and Tools. * List tools of data analysis that can be applied to text in any language, space, networks, images, and statistical analysis. * Evaluate existing digital platforms based on features that can be used for data analysis within different fields such as literature, history, art, and music. Acquiring, Cleaning, and Creating Data. * Identify the differences between unstructured, semi-structured, and structured data. * Practice different ways of downloading or creating data. * Apply command line functions to text files. * Create smaller text files from larger files using command line prompts. * Create data from multiple text files using Voyant. * Compare data results across text files using visualization in Voyant. ### Data Science: R Basics. Build a foundation in R and learn how to wrangle, analyze, and visualize data. ### Data Science: Visualization. Learn basic data visualization principles and how to apply them using ggplot2.

results.title: How to Evaluate Candidates Fairly and Consistently
results.content: # How can you ensure fair and consistent evaluation of candidates across different stages? But how can you ensure that you are evaluating them fairly and consistently across different stages of the hiring process? Here are some tips to help you reduce hiring bias and discrimination and improve your candidate selection. We should clearly define the skills, qualifications, and attributes that we are looking for in candidates and have a set of evaluation criteria that align with the requirements ,consistent evaluation process that is followed for all candidates at each stage This will help to eliminate the bias.Provide training to all evaluators involved in the hiring process and Use scorecard and assign scores and rank candidates accordingly involve multiple evaluators in the process and conduct calibration meetings among evaluators. Regularly review the evaluation criteria, processes, and outcomes to identify any potential biases or areas for improvement.Treat candidates with respect, provide timely updates. Implementing structured interviews with predetermined questions ensures each candidate receives fair and consistent evaluation. As a hiring manager, I believe that clear and objective criteria are crucial to ensure fair and consistent candidate evaluation. To ensure fair and consistent evaluation of candidates across different stages, I establish a structured evaluation framework that outlines specific criteria for each stage. Standardized scoring rubrics help assess candidates objectively based on skills, experience, and cultural fit. When evaluating candidates during the hiring process, it's important to use structured interviews to ensure fairness and consistency. By using structured interviews, we can improve the objectivity and reliability of our evaluation process and ultimately hire the best candidates for our organization. Another way to ensure fair and consistent evaluation of candidates is to involve multiple people in the hiring process. However, you should also ensure that everyone involved in the hiring process is aligned on the criteria, the process, and the expectations, and that they are trained on how to avoid bias and discrimination. In addition to using human judgment, you can also use data and evidence to evaluate candidates across different stages. You should solicit feedback from candidates, employees, and managers, on their experience and satisfaction with the hiring process.

results.title: RFP Scoring Matrix: How to Evaluate Proposals Fairly - Scopebird
results.content: # RFP Scoring Matrix: How to Evaluate Proposals Fairly. An RFP scoring matrix is a crucial tool that helps standardize the evaluation process, ensuring fairness, transparency, and efficiency. In this article, we will discuss how to create and use an RFP scoring matrix to evaluate proposals fairly. ## What is an RFP Scoring Matrix? An RFP scoring matrix is a structured framework that outlines the criteria and weights used to evaluate vendor proposals. This matrix typically includes various evaluation criteria, each with its own scoring scale and weight, reflecting the relative importance of each criterion to the project. ## Steps to Create an RFP Scoring Matrix. The first step in creating an RFP scoring matrix is to gather requirements from stakeholders and executives involved in the project. Common criteria include technical capabilities, vendor experience, project approach, total price, customer success practices, reputation, and data security. The scoring matrix is typically organized in a table format, with the evaluation criteria listed on one axis and the potential vendors on the other. Each cell in the matrix contains the score for a specific criterion for a particular vendor. For example, a detailed matrix might break down scoring to the question level, allowing for a nuanced evaluation of each proposal. In this method, proposals are first evaluated based on technical requirements. Only proposals that meet a minimum pass mark on the technical criteria proceed to the next stage, where they are evaluated based on cost. This method involves evaluating proposals based on technical requirements first, then calculating the cost per quality point. ## Best Practices for Using an RFP Scoring Matrix. Clearly communicate the evaluation criteria and weights to all vendors as part of the RFP documentation. First, evaluate proposals based on technical and quality criteria, setting a minimum threshold for qualification. ## Example of an RFP Scoring Matrix in Action. Here is an example of how an RFP scoring matrix might be used in practice:. Based on the weighted scores, Vendor C would be selected as the best proposal, having scored the highest overall. An RFP scoring matrix is an indispensable tool for ensuring fairness, transparency, and efficiency in the proposal evaluation process.

results.title: TRANSFORMATIONS a new journal on digital humanities - DARIAH-FI
results.content: Here is one to share your research with special interest in datasets, tools and workflows. *Transformations: A DARIAH Journal* is dedicated to providing a trusted, non-commercial platform for documenting various methodological and research activities in arts and humanities, including data gathering and processing, annotation and modeling, analysis and interpretation. Transformations embraces ephemeral or experimental scholarly outputs, including descriptions and analysis of data collections and workflows, annotation practices, software tools and training materials, as well as traditional scholarly papers. The first issue of *Transformations* is calling for contributions that explore, assess, and analyse the challenges of designing, implementing, documenting and sharing digitally-enabled workflows in the context of arts and humanities research. Submissions can take the form of classical research articles, project notes, tool descriptions, data papers, or workflow analyses. This issue invites contributions that address a variety of questions in terms of best practices: What is the state of the art in research workflows in the digital arts and humanities?

results.title: PhD Scholarship in Digital Arts and Humanities - Call for Applications - Moore Institute
results.content: # PhD Scholarship in Digital Arts and Humanities – Call for Applications. **PhD Scholarship in Digital Arts & Humanities**. NUI Galway invites applications for a four-year structured PhD scholarship in Digital Arts & Humanities to commence in September 2017. The Structured PhD in Digital Arts & Humanities at NUI Galway is a full-time four-year interdisciplinary programme from which seven students have graduated since its inception in 2011. Our ambition is for students to contribute to the developing digital arts and humanities community world-wide. The programme welcomes proposals on the use of digital tools and methodologies in the scholarly analysis of cultural texts and phenomena, and on practice-based research in digital art and media. 1. introduce students to the history of and theoretical issues in digital arts and humanities;. 2. provide the skills needed to apply advanced computational and information management paradigms to arts and/or humanities research;. Digital Humanities proposals should include a strong and clearly defined digital component, either as a core method of research and dissemination, or as a subject of research in itself. Proposals may address any topic within Digital Humanities, including (but not limited to): archives & preservation; authorship attribution; classical studies; corpus analysis; crowdsourcing; historical studies; interdisciplinary collaboration; internet history; literary studies; natural language processing; ontologies; scholarly editing; stylistics and stylometry; text-mining; textual studies; visualisation. Digital Arts proposals may examine questions such as artistic practice informed by digital media; the intersection between artistic creativity and technological innovation; or the impact of the digital on the form, structure, and function of narrative. Previous Digital Arts & Humanities PhD students have also worked closely with researchers at the Insight Centre for Data Analytics in Galway (). Prospective applicants are strongly advised to identify and correspond with potential supervisors for their research proposal before submitting a scholarship application:. 1. Description of proposed research (800 words). You should indicate the critical problems or research questions you propose to address in the thesis component of your PhD, as well as any digital outputs that may arise from your work. 5. Evidence of previous achievements in digital media or art practice (for practice-based PhD applicants *only*).
